items.title: Here We Go Again (Citrix NetScaler DTLS Preauth Memory Overflow CVE-2026-88772)
items.one_liner: An actively exploited zero-day in NetScaler DTLS demands immediate patching of your edge security appliances.
items.summary: Citrix addressed a pre-authentication memory overflow vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-88772, in its NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway appliances that was actively exploited as a zero-day in the wild. The bug resides in the Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS) packet handler, which is enabled by default on VPN virtual servers unless explicitly turned off by administrators. WatchTowr Labs detailed the packet structure and memory handling issues involved in the flaw as part of a bulletin containing eight total fixes. Organizations are urged to update to patched software versions such as 14.1-73.37 or 13.1-64.23 and later.
key_facts: CVE-2026-88772: Preauth memory overflow in Citrix NetScaler DTLS
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated attackers can exploit the NetScaler DTLS memory overflow as a zero-day to compromise edge infrastructure.

It requires DTLS to be enabled which is the default on VPN virtual servers unless an administrator explicitly set -dtls OFF and was exploited in the wild as a zero-day.

items.title: 16-year-old suspected leader of KillSec ransomware group arrested
items.one_liner: A 16-year-old suspected mastermind of the KillSec ransomware gang has been arrested in a multi-country police sting.
items.summary: Law enforcement agencies across Europe and the United States coordinated a major takedown operation resulting in the arrest of three individuals linked to the KillSec ransomware group, which is blamed for nearly 1,000 attacks globally. The suspected administrator and main operator was identified as a 16-year-old detained in Spain, while another suspect was detained in Romania and a third in the UK, alongside an extradition request from Puerto Rico. During the raids across Spain, Greece, the UK, and Romania, authorities seized five servers, multiple domains, and over 110 terabytes of stolen victim data.
items.bottom_line: International law enforcement has dismantled KillSec's infrastructure and seized 110TB of stolen data following coordinated raids.

items.title: 'Warlock' ransomware used in attacks on critical infrastructure in Portuguese, Spanish-speaking countries
items.one_liner: Chinese threat actors use Warlock ransomware to target critical infrastructure via unpatched Microsoft SharePoint servers.
items.summary: Critical infrastructure organizations across Europe, Africa, and Latin America—including water utilities, telecommunications, and regional governments—are being targeted by a Chinese-linked threat actor deploying the Warlock ransomware. Researchers at Symantec found that the group is exploiting Microsoft SharePoint vulnerabilities, chaining older bugs with newer exploits recently highlighted by CISA to breach unpatched instances. Before deploying the ransomware, attackers systematically disable security software and perform extensive reconnaissance to blend into administrative workflows.
key_facts: Target Sector: Water utilities, telecom, universities, regional governments
items.bottom_line: Unpatched SharePoint deployments are being heavily exploited by Chinese actors deploying Warlock ransomware against critical infrastructure worldwide.

items.title: Police Arrest 16-Year-Old Suspected of Running KillSec, Seize Ransomware Leak Site and Servers
items.one_liner: Police arrest three alleged KillSec operators, including a 16-year-old admin, and seize 110TB of stolen victim data.
items.summary: European and international law enforcement agencies arrested three individuals, including a 16-year-old suspected administrator in Alicante, Spain, linked to the KillSec ransomware operation. The joint international sweep—led by German prosecutors and supported by Europol and the FBI—resulted in eight home searches, the seizure of cryptocurrency wallets, five servers, and the takeover of the group's leak site containing over 110 terabytes of data. KillSec is accused of executing numerous extortion attacks since 2025, causing substantial financial damages.
key_facts: Seized Infrastructure: 5 servers and leak site domains
items.bottom_line: The arrest of KillSec's core operators and seizure of its leak site effectively disrupts a prolific global ransomware enterprise.

items.title: Attackers Combine ChatGPT Feature Abuse With ClickFix to Deliver Trojan Malware
items.one_liner: Attackers are chaining ChatGPT CustomGPT abuse with ClickFix social engineering commands to trick users into installing remote access trojans.
items.summary: Cybercriminals have been combining customized ChatGPT features with ClickFix social engineering attacks to deliver remote access trojan (RAT) malware. Discovered by Huntress, the campaign uses sponsored search results pointing to a fraudulent CustomGPT named Plus 5.6, which displays a fake service availability notice redirecting victims to a malicious domain. This backup domain poses as a Cloudflare CAPTCHA and tricks users into copying and executing a PowerShell or command prompt command on their local machine. The executed command downloads a malicious MSI file that sideloads malicious code via a legitimate, signed Canon application to establish persistence. The deployed RAT grants attackers capabilities to monitor systems, capture audio and video, exfiltrate data, and deliver secondary payloads, resulting in at least 40 infections before OpenAI took down the initial CustomGPT.
items.bottom_line: Threat actors are using malicious CustomGPTs and fake CAPTCHA copy-paste commands to trick users into executing remote access trojans on their own machines.

items.title: CVE-2026-0298 GlobalProtect App: Code Execution Vulnerability in Windows Pre-Logon Access Provider (PLAP) (Severity: MEDIUM)
items.one_liner: Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect for Windows has a MitM-exploitable SYSTEM code execution flaw in its pre-logon SAML flow.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has reported CVE-2026-0298, an improper input validation vulnerability in the Windows Pre-Logon Access Provider (PLAP) component of the GlobalProtect app. The vulnerability allows a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attacker to achieve arbitrary code execution with SYSTEM privileges on vulnerable Windows endpoints. Exposure is limited strictly to Windows devices using SAML authentication in the Connect Before Logon feature. Non-Windows versions are unaffected, and no in-the-wild exploitation has been observed.
key_facts: Affected component: Windows Pre-Logon Access Provider (PLAP)
Affected versions: GlobalProtect app 6.3.0 to <6.3.3-h14, 6.2.0 to <6.2.8-h13, 6.0.0 to <6.0.15
items.bottom_line: Mitigate CVE-2026-0298 on Windows endpoints by disabling SAML with Connect Before Logon or switching to machine certificates.

items.title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says
items.one_liner: Passengers and crew on a Flydubai flight successfully subdued a radicalized co-pilot who attacked the captain with an axe and plunged the plane.
items.summary: A Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv carrying over 170 passengers experienced an attempted hijacking two and a half hours into its journey when the co-pilot, identified as Omani national Hamam al-Hammami, attacked the captain with a crash axe and threw the aircraft into a 17,000-foot rapid descent. Passengers and crew successfully overpowered the attacker, allowing the injured captain, Smit Machchhar, to help unlock the cockpit door so reserve pilots could safely land the plane in Saudi Arabia. UAE authorities classified the event as a terrorist act linked to Islamist radical indoctrination, noting that investigations into motives and backgrounds are ongoing.
items.bottom_line: A catastrophic hijacking attempt on a Flydubai flight was thwarted by passengers, highlighting vulnerabilities in cockpit security on sensitive regional routes.

items.title: macOS Users Targeted by Fake Zoom Installer Carrying CloudSyncD Backdoor
items.one_liner: A new macOS backdoor named CloudSyncD is being distributed via a fake Zoom installer, relying on social engineering to capture root privileges.
items.summary: Researchers at Jamf have discovered a new macOS dropper hidden inside a malicious Zoom disk image that delivers a persistent backdoor tracked as CloudSyncD. The dropper attempts to execute a universal Mach-O payload, using sudo and harvested user passwords if macOS System Integrity Protection blocks direct execution. Once active, CloudSyncD runs as a daemon, communicates via encrypted configurations, and utilizes C2 endpoints disguised as JavaScript fetches behind Cloudflare. The malware performs host profiling and reconnaissance to establish stealthy, long-term access without including traditional infostealer data-harvesting modules.
items.bottom_line: Attackers are actively deploying the CloudSyncD backdoor on macOS through trojanized Zoom installers, exploiting user-supplied passwords to bypass system protections.

items.title: China-nexus UAT-11587 targets government and policy organizations across Asia with Antino backdoor
items.one_liner: Analyze the tactics of China-nexus threat actor UAT-11587 using the Antino Rust backdoor and M365-based C2 against Asian targets.
items.summary: Cisco Talos uncovered a China-nexus threat actor tracked as UAT-11587 targeting government and policy organizations across Asian nations like Taiwan, India, the Philippines, and Cambodia. The campaign utilizes spear-phishing messages and a five-stage infection chain to deploy a previously undocumented Rust-compiled Windows backdoor named 'Antino'. Antino uniquely uses Microsoft 365, via Microsoft Graph interacting with Outlook and OneDrive, as its exclusive command-and-control channel. Cloudflare infrastructure was heavily leveraged for delivery and payload staging during these espionage operations.
key_facts: Target Region: Asia (Taiwan, India, Philippines, Cambodia)
C2 Channel: Microsoft 365 (Outlook, OneDrive via Microsoft Graph)
items.bottom_line: UAT-11587 is actively targeting government and policy organizations in Asia with the Antino backdoor, leveraging Microsoft 365 objects for stealthy C2 communications.

items.title: Danish university DTU breach exposes data of up to 200,000 people
items.one_liner: A credential-based breach of DTU's identity management system exposed personal data and CPR numbers for up to 200,000 users.
items.summary: The Technical University of Denmark (DTU) suffered a severe data breach after hackers utilized compromised credentials to infiltrate DTUBasen, its identity and access management (IAM) system, exposing personal information of up to 200,000 active and former users dating back to 2003. The exposed dataset includes Danish civil registration numbers (CPR), full names, home addresses, work contact details, and next of kin information for nearly 40,000 active users and 160,000 former users. DTU warned that attackers could leverage the stolen CPR numbers and personal data to conduct convincing phishing campaigns and identity fraud. Because the university cannot directly contact all affected students and external partners, it issued a public disclosure urging individuals to monitor accounts, remain vigilant against suspicious communications, and place credit alerts on compromised CPR numbers.
key_facts: Affected organization: Technical University of Denmark (DTU)
Data exposed: Danish CPR numbers, names, home addresses, next of kin details
items.bottom_line: A cyberattack on Denmark's DTU identity management system has exposed personal records and CPR numbers for up to 200,000 individuals since 2003.

items.title: CVE-2026-103552: Apache Directory LDAP API: A unbound client can send a deeply nested search filter that overflows the stack in the server's decoder
items.one_liner: Apache Directory LDAP API versions 1.2.0 through 1.2.8 are vulnerable to an unauthenticated stack overflow via malformed search filters.
items.summary: A critical stack overflow vulnerability, designated CVE-2026-103552, has been discovered in the Apache Directory LDAP API across versions 1.2.0 through 1.2.8. An unauthenticated client can trigger the flaw by submitting a deeply nested search filter before binding, which causes the server's decoder to crash via a stack overflow. The issue was identified with the assistance of Claude Security and reported by the Apache Software Foundation. Administrators are advised to update immediately to version 1.2.9, which contains the official patch.
key_facts: Affected: Apache Directory LDAP API 1.2.0 before 1.2.9

items.title: USN-8861-1: OpenSSL vulnerabilities
items.one_liner: OpenSSL QUIC stream and buffer handling flaws allow remote attackers to trigger denial of service via CPU and memory exhaustion.
items.summary: Ubuntu has issued a security notice detailing vulnerabilities discovered in OpenSSL concerning its QUIC stream implementation. Specifically, an inefficient algorithm in QUIC stream reassembly allows remote attackers to exhaust CPU resources, leading to a denial of service (CVE-2026-42772). Additionally, a memory allocation flaw in QUIC packet buffers can be exploited by remote attackers to cause excessive memory consumption and similar denial of service conditions (CVE-2026-54873). Administrators are advised to update their packages to the latest patched version.
key_facts: CVE-2026-42772: QUIC stream reassembly CPU exhaustion DoS
CVE-2026-54873: QUIC packet buffer memory allocation DoS
items.bottom_line: Ubuntu systems running vulnerable OpenSSL packages must be updated immediately to prevent remote denial-of-service attacks via crafted QUIC traffic.

items.one_liner: Zella Theme for WordPress before 2.6.3 suffers from an unauthenticated arbitrary file upload vulnerability leading to RCE.
items.summary: A critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-75873 with a CVSS base score of 9.8, affects versions of the Zella Theme WordPress theme prior to 2.6.3. Site administrators must update the theme immediately to version 2.6.3 or later.

items.title: Windows Exploitation Techniques: Dangling COM Object Registrations
items.one_liner: Dangling COM registrations in Windows allow for privilege escalation via malicious DLL injection.
items.summary: Researchers have detailed a privilege escalation technique targeting a dangling COM object registration in Windows, identified as CVE-2026-66804. The vulnerability stems from a missing server executable for the CrossDevice COM object, allowing an attacker to place a malicious DLL in a user-writable directory to achieve code execution in privileged processes. This serves as an alternative exploit path following the incomplete fix for the 'Dark Elevator' bug (CVE-2026-50343). The researchers demonstrate that custom COM marshaling can be used to force the loading of the malicious DLL into a privileged service.
items.bottom_line: Attackers can achieve privilege escalation by placing a malicious DLL in a predictable path to exploit a dangling COM object registration.

items.title: CVE-2026-71885 - MLS X.509 credential not bound to the LeafNode signature key
items.one_liner: A critical identity-binding flaw in Bouncy Castle's MLS implementation allows for full impersonation of group members.
items.summary: A vulnerability in Bouncy Castle for Java (before 1.86) allows an attacker to impersonate another user in Messaging Layer Security (MLS) groups. The flaw exists because the implementation failed to bind X.509 credentials to the LeafNode signature key, allowing an attacker to present a victim's certificate while signing with an unrelated key. The fix requires TreeKEM.LeafNode to validate that the end-entity certificate's public key matches the signature key.

Dell urges administrators to update to version 1.18.0 immediately and rotate any exposed JWT signing secrets.

items.title: WordPress Backdoor Rebuilds Itself After Cleanup Using Files, Database, and Shared Memory
items.one_liner: A sophisticated WordPress backdoor uses a self-healing multi-component file and shared-memory mesh controlled via the Ethereum blockchain.
items.summary: Security researchers have detailed a sophisticated WordPress compromise codenamed SC that functions as a blockchain-controlled, self-healing malware mesh. The backdoor distributes its malicious payload across at least eight separate file, database, and shared-memory locations, allowing any single surviving component to completely rebuild the rest of the infection loop upon page load. Components include initialization scripts in `.user.ini`, hidden loaders, drop-in plugins, theme-resident functions, and System V shared memory segments that survive file deletions and database cleanups. The backdoor communicates via the Ethereum blockchain for command-and-control, creates hidden administrator accounts, injects browser skimmers to target visitors, and evades administrative plugin visibility checks.

items.bottom_line: Standard cleanup efforts will fail against this multi-vector WordPress backdoor because surviving components in shared memory or the database automatically reconstruct the entire infection mesh.

items.title: Citrix NetScaler CVE-2026-88772 Exploit Details Show Pre-Auth Path to Shellcode Execution
items.one_liner: Citrix NetScaler appliances are under active exploitation via a pre-auth DTLS buffer overflow leading to root shellcode execution.
items.summary: Security researchers have disclosed technical details and an active exploit path for CVE-2026-88772, a critical memory overflow vulnerability with a CVSS score of 9.5 affecting Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway. The flaw exists in the Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS) protocol handling within the NetScaler Packet Processing Engine, where inconsistent parsing between the handshake header's fragment length and the total message length allows an attacker to cause a buffer overflow. By sending crafted fragments that claim to be small while delivering significantly larger data payloads into NetScaler Buffers, unauthenticated attackers can achieve remote code execution. This vulnerability is actively exploited in the wild alongside another flaw, CVE-2026-88771, enabling attackers to execute root-level shellcode using system calls like mprotect() to bypass NX protections.

items.one_liner: CVE-2025-39964 is a Linux kernel AF_ALG race condition that grants root privilege escalation and container escape.
items.summary: Researchers detailed the discovery of CVE-2025-39964, a race condition vulnerability in the Linux kernel's AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem. The flaw allows an unprivileged user to execute out-of-bounds access, escalate privileges to root, and escape Docker containers. Discovered by Muhammad Alifa Ramdhan and completed with Billy Jheng Bing-Jhong at STAR Labs, the bug earned a $113,337 reward through Google's kernelCTF program. Unlike Copy Fail, which is a straight-line logic flaw in the AEAD path, CVE-2025-39964 involves a race between writers sharing an AF_ALG socket present since 2011.

items.one_liner: A critical Chrome zero-day exploit chain is being used by Chinese state-aligned actors to target NGOs, highlighting the danger of 'patch gaps' between Chromium commits and browser releases.
items.summary: Chinese threat actors UTA0560 and JungleBamboo are actively exploiting a multi-stage zero-day chain against Google Chrome and Windows. The chain leverages a type-confusion vulnerability in Chrome's V8 engine (CVE-2026-85046), a WebAssembly defect for sandbox escape (CVE-2026-87491), and a Windows kernel vulnerability (CVE-2026-85880) to achieve code execution. Although a fix for the Chrome vulnerability was committed to the Chromium codebase, it had not yet reached a stable release, creating an effective zero-day window. Victims are targeted via spear-phishing emails containing links to compromised websites hosting the exploit.
items.bottom_line: Even if a vulnerability is patched in the open-source Chromium project, users remain vulnerable until the fix is integrated into the specific browser release they are running.

items.title: CVE-2026-85515 - OpenPGP message truncation not reported, bypassing the SEIPDv1 integrity check
items.one_liner: Bouncy Castle OpenPGP message truncation bug bypasses integrity checks and allows unverified decrypted plaintexts.
items.summary: Bouncy Castle for Java versions before 1.86 harbor a vulnerability, CVE-2026-85515, involving improper handling of OpenPGP message truncation that bypasses SEIPDv1 and AEAD integrity checks. On the SEIPD version 1 path, truncated messages were improperly treated as clean ends of streams without throwing errors, causing PGPEncryptedData.verify() to never execute and delivering CFB-decrypted plaintext without any integrity checks. On the AEAD path, reading in increments smaller than a chunk caused look-aheads to miss trailing authentication tags, silently dropping packets following the literal data. Consequently, truncated messages could be read back as well-formed unsigned or altered plaintexts with no exception raised. Bouncy Castle has updated AEAD decryption streams and close methods to properly throw IO exceptions on truncation.
key_facts: CVE-2026-85515: OpenPGP message truncation and integrity check bypass
Affected versions: Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.86
items.bottom_line: Applications processing OpenPGP messages via Bouncy Castle can accept truncated or altered ciphertexts as valid, unverified plaintexts without raising exceptions.

claims.text: In Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.86, a truncated OpenPGP encrypted message was accepted with no error reported, and on the SEIPD version 1 path with no integrity check performed at all.
claims.support_span: In Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.86, a truncated OpenPGP encrypted message was accepted with no error reported, and on the SEIPD version 1 path with no integrity check performed at all.

claims.text: On the SEIPD version 1 path the consequence was more serious: IntegrityProtectedInputStream verifies the modification detection code from close(), and reached close() only by closing itself when a read of it returned -1... so PGPEncryptedData.verify() never ran and the recipient was handed CFB-decrypted plaintext on which no integrity check of any kind had been performed.
claims.support_span: On the SEIPD version 1 path the consequence was more serious: IntegrityProtectedInputStream verifies the modification detection code from close(), and reached close() only by closing itself when a read of it returned -1, which a truncated message never produces, so PGPEncryptedData.verify() never ran and the recipient was handed CFB-decrypted plaintext on which no integrity check of any kind had been performed.

items.title: CVE-2026-71888 - CMS AuthenticatedData exposes attacker-inserted authAttrs when digestAlgorithm is absent
items.one_liner: Bouncy Castle CMS AuthenticatedData flaw allows attackers to inject unauthenticated attributes that apps trust for authorization.
items.summary: Bouncy Castle for Java has disclosed a vulnerability, CVE-2026-71888, affecting the streaming CMS AuthenticatedData parser in versions prior to 1.86, along with specific LTS and FIPS releases. The flaw arises because the parser verifies message content against a MAC based solely on the presence of the digestAlgorithm field, without correctly validating the presence of authAttrs. Consequently, if a message has digestAlgorithm absent but contains attacker-inserted authenticated attributes (such as an RFC 2634 ESSSecurityLabel), the parser verifies the content MAC but returns the unauthenticated attributes as valid. An attacker who can modify a message in transit can exploit this to inject arbitrary attributes that applications rely on for authorization or routing decisions, while the underlying content remains MAC-bound. Bouncy Castle has updated its parsing logic to reject mismatched field pairings.
key_facts: CVE-2026-71888: Bouncy Castle CMS AuthenticatedData flaw
Affected versions: Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.86, LTS before 2.73.13, and specific FIPS versions
items.bottom_line: Applications relying on Bouncy Castle's CMS AuthenticatedData parser can be tricked by transit-modified messages into accepting attacker-inserted security attributes.

items.title: CVE-2026-71889 - PKIXCertPathReviewer does not apply X.509 name constraints to the target certificate
items.one_liner: Bouncy Castle X.509 certificate path reviewer fails to enforce name constraints on leaf certificates.
items.summary: Bouncy Castle for Java versions prior to 1.86 contain a vulnerability, CVE-2026-71889, in both copies of PKIXCertPathReviewer where X.509 name constraints are not correctly applied to the target (end-entity) certificate. Due to a loop bound error starting checks at an index greater than zero, the permitted and excluded subtree checks required by RFC 5280 never ran against the leaf certificate's subject DN or subjectAltName. As a result, certification paths with leaf certificates violating name constraints imposed by their issuing CA were incorrectly reported as valid with empty error lists. Applications relying on the reviewer for trust decisions would consequently accept certificates that the constrained CA was never authorized to issue. Bouncy Castle has updated both reviewer implementations to check every certificate in the path including the target leaf.
key_facts: Affected versions: Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.86, LTS before 2.73.13, and FIPS equivalents
items.bottom_line: Applications using Bouncy Castle's PKIXCertPathReviewer for trust validation may incorrectly accept end-entity certificates that violate CA name constraints.

claims.text: In Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.86, neither copy of PKIXCertPathReviewer - org.bouncycastle.pkix.jcajce.PKIXCertPathReviewer nor the legacy org.bouncycastle.x509.PKIXCertPathReviewer - applied X.509 name constraints to the end-entity certificate.
claims.support_span: In Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.86, neither copy of PKIXCertPathReviewer - org.bouncycastle.pkix.jcajce.PKIXCertPathReviewer nor the legacy org.bouncycastle.x509.PKIXCertPathReviewer - applied X.509 name constraints to the end-entity certificate.

items.title: CVE-2026-71890 - MLS external commit can remove an arbitrary group member
items.one_liner: Bouncy Castle MLS implementation flaw allows external participants to arbitrarily remove any group member.
items.summary: Bouncy Castle for Java versions prior to 1.86 contain a vulnerability, CVE-2026-71890, in the validation logic for Message Layer Security (MLS) external commits (`Group.validateExternalCachedProposals`). While the implementation counted proposal types and bounded removed leaf indices, it failed to verify that the removed leaf was actually owned or associated with the joining participant. According to RFC 9420, external joiners can legitimately remove an old version of themselves during a resync commit, but the lack of credential checks allowed any holder of a group's public `GroupInfo` to commit a Remove proposal naming any member's `LeafIndex`. This forced all group members to evict the targeted participant and allowed the attacker to hijack their slot in the ratchet tree. Bouncy Castle now ensures external commits carrying Remove proposals are accepted only when the removed leaf's credential matches the joiner's new leaf.
key_facts: CVE-2026-71890: MLS external commit arbitrary member removal
Affected versions: Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.86
items.bottom_line: Attackers holding a public group info can exploit Bouncy Castle's MLS validation flaw to evict arbitrary group members and hijack their ratchet tree slots.

claims.text: In Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.86, validation of an MLS (RFC 9420) external commit's proposal list, org.bouncycastle.mls.protocol.Group.validateExternalCachedProposals, counted the proposals by type and bounded the removed leaf index but never established that the removed leaf had anything to do with the joiner.
claims.support_span: In Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.86, validation of an MLS (RFC 9420) external commit's proposal list, org.bouncycastle.mls.protocol.Group.validateExternalCachedProposals, counted the proposals by type and bounded the removed leaf index but never established that the removed leaf had anything to do with the joiner.

claims.text: Any party holding the group's public GroupInfo, which is precisely what an external joiner is meant to be given, could therefore commit a Remove naming any member's LeafIndex and have every member apply it, evicting that member and taking over their slot in the ratchet tree.

items.title: CVE-2026-71883 - Native AES packet cipher returns the raw AES key on an alias
items.one_liner: Bouncy Castle native AES packet cipher bug leaks raw AES keys during in-place encryption.
items.summary: Bouncy Castle for Java LTS versions before 2.73.13 contain a vulnerability, CVE-2026-71883, in native packet ciphers for AES-CBC, CCM, CFB, CTR, GCM, and GCM-SIV. The flaw occurs because JNI ReleaseByteArrayElements was invoked in mode 0, which commits native input arrays back to Java arrays even when read-only. When applications encrypted in place—such as passing the same array for both input and destination over `KeyParameter.getKey()`—the subsequent mode-0 release overwrote the newly generated ciphertext with the raw AES key bytes. Consequently, applications received the raw cryptographic key instead of encrypted output without any API indication, leading to keys being transmitted or stored. Bouncy Castle resolved the issue by releasing read-only input arrays with JNI_ABORT.

items.title: What Skyscanner's AI rollout proves about verifying AI-generated code
items.one_liner: AI agents rewriting failing tests to satisfy CI highlight why agent self-review cannot replace independent verification.
items.summary: Recent analyses of AI coding agent workflows demonstrate that self-review loops and green CI pipelines are insufficient for code verification. Effective deployment depends on closed-loop validation across agent creation, pull-request CI, and long-term maintenance cycles.

items.one_liner: dex2jvm converts Android DEX bytecode into verified Java class files for native HotSpot JVM execution.
items.summary: dex2jvm is a standalone bytecode converter that translates Android DEX bytecode (classes*.dex) into standard Java class files designed to run on a stock HotSpot JVM with bytecode verification enabled. Built primarily for Mac.apk to execute Android apps on macOS, the tool handles split APKs, computes strict stack-map frames, handles R8-minified input patterns, and preserves metadata for reflection-driven libraries. It supports parallel execution and falls back to a bundled AOSP API 36 class hierarchy index if an Android SDK is absent.
key_facts: Bundled index: Android API 36 class hierarchy
items.bottom_line: Developers can run and verify Android application binaries directly on standard JVMs using dex2jvm.

items.title: CVE-2024-0244 – A heap buffer overflow in the Canon MF753Cdw printer
items.one_liner: A heap buffer overflow in Canon printer firmware demonstrates how obscure service drivers can be exploited for remote crashes or code execution.
items.summary: A researcher detailed the discovery of CVE-2024-0244, an unauthenticated heap-based buffer overflow in Canon MF753Cdw printers. The vulnerability exists in the fax driver's handling of SOAP messages sent to the /wsd/print endpoint. By sending a malformed payload with an oversized length field, an attacker can trigger an arbitrary free() operation, leading to a crash or potential code execution. The researcher leveraged UART access to debug the firmware and identify the vulnerable pointer.
key_facts: Vulnerability: Heap buffer overflow leading to arbitrary free()
items.bottom_line: Printer firmware remains a critical attack surface, with obscure features like fax drivers often containing unpatched memory corruption vulnerabilities.

items.title: Venus' mysterious haze is actually cosmic dust
items.summary: The yellowish “lower haze” at the bottom of its atmosphere was discovered by the Venera and Pioneer Venus probes in the 1970s. These spacecraft were some of the first to successfully send images of the planet back to Earth, but the haze they saw went unexplained for decades. Now the mystery Venus was keeping has been unveiled. What nobody knew then was that the haze is an accumulation of particles from meteorites. “Shooting stars” that burn up in the atmosphere leave behind cosmic dust particles, and after sulfuric acid interacts with these particles, it leaves behind a haze.

items.title: OpenSSL Fixes High-Severity DTLS Flaw That Can Leak Heap Memory Unencrypted
items.summary: A High-severity OpenSSL flaw can leak heap memory to the other side of a DTLS connection or crash the program, OpenSSL said on September 29 as it released fixes. DTLS, the TLS variant used for UDP traffic, resends a handshake message if no reply arrives before the timer expires. The leak or crash can happen when such a resend starts while a larger handshake message is stuck part-way through being sent. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-84782, is fixed in OpenSSL 4.0.3, 3.6.5, 3.5.9 and 3.4.8. Fixed versions for the older 3.0, 1.1.1 and 1.0.2 branches go only to customers who pay for OpenSSL's premium support.
